package_organization.issue_character: The base/ package acts as an undifferentiated monolith containing 60+ models, 40+ services, and cross-cutting helpers with no internal grouping by domain, causing high cognitive overhead and difficult ownership assignment.
package_organization.score_rationale: The outer Django-app structure is reasonable but the internal layout of base/ is severely overloaded: 60+ model files and 40+ service files in flat directories spanning ticketing, conferencing, video, seating, and chat represent a flat directory overload that the rubric flags. Additionally, common/ and eventyay_common/ have ambiguous, overlapping boundaries, and core/ holds only 2 utility files. The codebase is significantly above trivial size (>200 production files) so flatness is not justified by scale. Score reflects many confirmed overload signals partially offset by coherent outer app boundaries.

issues.summary: base/models/ flat directory overload — 60+ files spanning 6+ distinct domains
evidence: 60+ model files in a single flat directory; domains present: ticketing (orders, product, vouchers, tax, invoices), conferencing (submission, schedule, slot, track), chat (chat, channel, membership), video (bbb, janus, streaming, stream_schedule, turn), seating (seating, room, roomquestion), exhibitor (exhibitor, poster, roulette)
issues.suggestion: Staged reorg plan: (1) Create subdirectories: base/models/ticketing/, base/models/conferencing/, base/models/chat/, base/models/video/, base/models/seating/. (2) Move files by domain affinity. (3) Update __init__.py imports to preserve the flat public API surface (no callers need to change). (4) Validate with 'python -c "from eventyay.base.models import *"' and run pytest tests/ to confirm no import regressions. Do this in a single PR per subdomain to keep diffs reviewable.

issues.summary: base/services/ flat directory overload — 40 service files across distinct domains
evidence: 40 service files in a flat directory; domains overlap with base/models/ — chat, video (bbb, janus, turn), ticketing (orders, cart, invoices, vouchers, pricing), conferencing (teams, shredder)
issues.suggestion: Mirror the model subdirectory split in services/: base/services/ticketing/, base/services/conferencing/, base/services/chat/, base/services/video/. Move files and update all importers. Use 'grep -r "from eventyay.base.services" app/' to enumerate callers before moving. Validate with pytest tests/.

issues.summary: common/ and eventyay_common/ have overlapping, ambiguous responsibilities
evidence: common/ contains: context_processors, exceptions, image, mail, text, urls, views/mixins
eventyay_common/ contains: views/account, views/organizer, views/event, views/team — all are event-management UI views, not 'common' utilities
The split suggests eventyay_common/ holds a specific subdomain (organizer/account UI) rather than shared infrastructure
issues.suggestion: Rename eventyay_common/ to a more descriptive package (e.g., account/ or eventyay_admin/) reflecting its actual contents. Then audit common/ to ensure it contains only genuinely cross-cutting utilities. Run 'grep -r "eventyay_common" app/' to enumerate import sites before renaming.

issues.summary: core/ is a thin straggler package with only 2 utility files
evidence: core/utils/ contains exactly 2 files (redis.py, statsd.py); helpers/ already exists for cross-cutting utilities
Dedicated 'core' namespace implies architectural centrality but delivers only two infrastructure helpers
issues.suggestion: Move core/utils/redis.py and core/utils/statsd.py into helpers/ (or helpers/infra/). Update importers with 'grep -r "from eventyay.core" app/'. Remove the now-empty core/ package to eliminate the ambiguous boundary.

root_causes: base/ accumulated files from two legacy systems (pretix + pretalx) without a post-merge reorganization pass
No enforced package boundary policy during the platform merger meant files landed in whichever existing directory seemed closest
possible_false_positives: helpers/ mixing stripe_utils — stripe is third-party but may be the only payment integration, making helpers/ an acceptable home for it
